title: The Lion and the Eagle
summary: A lion declined an alliance with an eagle: "How can I trust a partner whose wings can carry him to the clouds while I am bound to the earth?"...
full_text: A lion declined an alliance with an eagle: "How can I trust a partner whose wings can carry him to the clouds while I am bound to the earth?"
moral: Do not ally with one who can fly away when oaths are tested.
image_alt: The Lion and the Eagle illustration from the Aesop's Fables collection.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Lion and the Eagle"?
options: Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.

author: Aesop (~620–564 BCE / Trans. George Fyler Townsend)
content_notes: Family-safe traditional adaptation from the Aesop's Fables anthology.

vocabulary.meaning: wise advice given to guide decisions
the ability to judge well and understand the truth
the ability to remain calm and think clearly during sudden events
